clinicalPearls: Caused by variants in GRIN2A encoding the GluN2A subunit of the NMDA-type glutamate receptor, a channel central to excitatory synaptic transmission and developmental plasticity.

GRIN2A is the principal genetic cause of the epilepsy-aphasia spectrum, spanning benign childhood epilepsy with centrotemporal spikes at the mild end to Landau-Kleffner syndrome and epileptic encephalopathy with continuous spike-and-wave in sleep at the severe end.

Speech and language impairment is a defining and sometimes dominant feature, including acquired auditory verbal agnosia, expressive dysfunction, and dyspraxia, which can persist even after seizures remit.
The EEG hallmark is prominent, often sleep-activated, centrotemporal or more diffuse epileptiform discharges, with electrical status epilepticus in sleep marking the severe end.
Functional consequences of variants differ: both gain-of-function and loss-of-function changes occur, which has driven interest in mechanism-directed therapy rather than a single treatment for all.
Seizures are frequently focal with orofacial and speech-arrest features and may be relatively infrequent despite marked cognitive and language impact.
Variants may be de novo or inherited with variable expressivity, so relatives can be mildly affected or unaffected carriers.
Because language regression can outlast seizures, monitoring and supporting communication is as important as seizure control.
reference.pathophysiology: GRIN2A encodes GluN2A, a regulatory subunit of the N-methyl-D-aspartate (NMDA) glutamate receptor, a ligand- and voltage-gated cation channel that mediates calcium-permeable excitatory neurotransmission and underpins synaptic plasticity and cortical maturation, with particularly important roles in perisylvian language networks. Disease-causing variants disturb receptor function in mechanistically opposite ways: gain-of-function changes increase channel open probability, agonist potency, or calcium flux and prolong excitatory currents, while loss-of-function changes (including truncating and destabilising missense variants) reduce receptor availability or current, and either can perturb the excitation-inhibition balance during critical developmental windows. This dysregulated NMDA-receptor signalling in maturing cortical and language-related circuits produces the characteristic sleep-activated epileptiform activity and the disproportionate, sometimes acquired, impairment of speech and language that defines the epilepsy-aphasia spectrum. The bidirectional functional impact is clinically important because it underlies attempts to tailor therapy — for instance considering receptor modulation according to whether a variant enhances or diminishes channel function — rather than applying a uniform approach.
additionalDifferentials: Idiopathic (self-limited) epilepsy with centrotemporal spikes without a GRIN2A variant
Landau-Kleffner syndrome of other or unknown genetic cause
Other genetic causes of encephalopathy with electrical status epilepticus in sleep
Autism spectrum disorder with language regression
Acquired epileptic aphasia secondary to structural lesions
Other GRIN-family disorders such as GRIN1 and GRIN2B related conditions
additionalInvestigations: Gene-panel or exome/genome sequencing including GRIN2A and related NMDA-receptor genes
Sleep-deprived and overnight EEG to detect sleep-activated discharges and spike-wave activation in sleep
Formal speech, language, and auditory-processing assessment including auditory verbal agnosia testing
MRI brain to exclude structural lesions
Neuropsychological and cognitive evaluation over time
Audiological assessment to distinguish peripheral hearing loss from central auditory agnosia
Parental testing to clarify inheritance and expressivity
redFlags: Acquired loss or regression of previously established language, especially auditory verbal agnosia
EEG showing marked activation of epileptiform discharges in sleep or electrical status epilepticus in sleep
Progressive cognitive or behavioural deterioration accompanying the epileptiform activity
Seizure worsening or new deficits following an antiseizure medication change
Marked functional communication decline despite few or no clinically apparent seizures
reference.prognosis: Outcome spans a wide spectrum: milder cases resemble self-limited focal epilepsy of childhood with good seizure remission, whereas severe cases with electrical status epilepticus in sleep or Landau-Kleffner syndrome may leave lasting language and cognitive impairment even after seizures resolve. Long-term language and educational support is often needed regardless of eventual seizure freedom.
pitfalls: Attributing acquired language regression to primary autism or hearing loss and missing the underlying epileptic aphasia.
Relying on a routine waking EEG and failing to capture sleep-activated discharges or spike-wave in sleep.
Assuming a uniformly benign course because the disorder overlaps with self-limited centrotemporal-spike epilepsy.
Applying one antiseizure strategy without considering whether the variant is gain- or loss-of-function.
Focusing on seizure counts while underappreciating the disproportionate language and cognitive morbidity.
references: International consensus guidance on genetic epilepsies
management: Treat seizures with antiseizure medication such as valproate, levetiracetam or sulthiame, tailored to the epilepsy phenotype
Manage electrical status epilepticus in sleep and continuous spike-and-wave in sleep with corticosteroid courses, benzodiazepines or other immunomodulatory antiseizure regimens
Consider mechanism-directed therapy with an NMDA-receptor antagonist such as memantine for characterised gain-of-function variants under specialist guidance
Provide intensive speech and language therapy for auditory verbal agnosia and expressive and dyspraxic impairment
Offer educational support and neuropsychological input for cognitive and language difficulties
Monitor with serial and sleep-recorded EEG and repeated developmental and language assessment
Provide genetic counselling, noting that most variants are de novo dominant while some loss-of-function GRIN2A pedigrees are inherited, and evaluate at-risk relatives
